title: [Spec] Windowed draft-decode attention for built-in EAGLE / MTP drafts (sglang #32673)
quote: `W=4032 S=64` (4096 prefix entries per draft step), batch 1, RULER
proves: Merged 2026-09-22: optional sliding-window plus attention-sink KV read for the EAGLE/MTP draft decode step; target still verifies at full attention. W=4032 S=64, batch 1, RULER. Acceptance length native->window 3.25->3.28 at 32K and 5.49->5.49 at 256K on Triton; FlashInfer 3.28->3.28 at 32K, 5.39->5.37 at 256K. PR also says "a 4% per-iteration saving against a 4% acceptance dip" and "Acceptance never beats native in this sweep."
does_not_prove: Claim supported but the 3.25->3.28 and 5.49 numbers are Triton-only; batch 1 only. Says nothing about draft-state catch-up after K=0 or about rebuilding draft KV from a window.
bearing: C3' prior art: windowed draft KV read exists in SGLang; narrows C3' to the catch-up/rebuild case

title: [Bugfix] Keep draft KV in sync when dynamic K is zero (vllm-metal #716)
quote: Keep the draft model KV cache synchronized when dynamic speculative decoding selects zero speculative tokens for a batch.
proves: At K=0 draft token generation is skipped but draft cache ingestion runs. Description reports cold acceptance 28/57 (49.12%) before vs 36/39 after. Eager ingest was about 10-11% more wall time; follow-up #734 lazy catch-up cut median wall time 0.8610 s -> 0.7754 s (9.94%) and ingest tokens 58.09%.
does_not_prove: Acceptance gain is contested: reviewer ricky-chaoju "couldn't reproduce the acceptance part"; author says it depends on a request first seen during a K=0 prefill. The ~10% is the cost of eager sync (and the lazy saving), not a stale-KV penalty. Plain draft-model KV, not EAGLE-3/DFlash hidden-state drafters.
bearing: C3' direct prior art on vllm-metal (eager then lazy catch-up); shrinks C3' gap

title: [Spec Decode] Use scheduler-owned lookahead for draft-model KV (vllm-metal #843)
quote: This PR uses the scheduler's block table for committed and lookahead writes.
proves: Merged 2026-09-27. Serving comparison against upstream bd8619c: 96/96 exact with identical acceptance/rejection counts. A commit compares draft tokens and physical paged KV "after rejection, deferred zero-K ingest, and page reassignment."
does_not_prove: 96/96 is vs upstream vllm-metal, not vs target-only generation (only 66/96 exact there). Draft-model KV only, not EAGLE-3/DFlash.
bearing: C3' prior art (deferred K=0 ingest tested); C7' supports: exact-equivalence check used in practice and fails vs target-only

title: [spec decoding] supports step 0 in adaptive spec decoding (sglang #23994)
quote: supports step 0 in adaptive spec decoding (updating draft kv cache without draft decoding)
proves: Merged 2026-06-16; adds a step-0 mode to SGLang adaptive spec decoding that updates draft KV without draft decoding.
does_not_prove: Motivation and Modifications sections are empty: no mechanism, cost, or acceptance numbers given. No windowed rebuild.
bearing: C3' prior art: SGLang keeps draft KV current at K=0 (eager)

title: feat(spec): give an EAGLE-3 draft layer the sliding window its config declares (tokenspeed #2355)
quote: The edited draft was not trained with a 128-token window, so its lower acceptance is expected;
proves: Unmodified draft acceptance 2.195 vs 2.195 (main vs PR); draft labeled with a 128-token sliding window gets acceptance 1.97 on the same weights.
does_not_prove: No run with a window-trained draft, so the window is the likely but not isolated cause. Page model name for GPT-OSS-120B was not confirmed in my fetch output. Not a K=0 catch-up study.
bearing: C3' risk: an untrained window costs ~10% acceptance; windowed rebuild may need training

title: Eagle3DecodingConfig (TensorRT-LLM LLM API reference)
quote: Batch sizes 33+: use draft_len=0 (implicit, speculation disabled).
proves: draft_len_schedule example maps batch 33+ to draft_len=0; acceptance_rate_threshold disables speculation permanently once the rolling average of accepted/drafted over acceptance_rate_window_size falls below it (window 0 or unset disables the feature).
does_not_prove: draft_len=0 for 33+ is an example in the field doc, not a default. Says nothing about draft KV state at draft_len=0 or on resume; the kill switch is permanent, so there is no resume.
bearing: C3' context: K=0 regimes exist in TRT-LLM; permanent kill switch avoids the resume problem

title: [Feature]: Measure the Dynamic SD table instead of writing it by hand (vllm #62740)
quote: On an H100, a table at K=0 ran 19–22% slower than no speculation.
proves: Author states "K=0 still runs EAGLE-style drafters, so it is not the same as speculation off" and a K=0 table ran 19-22% slower than no speculation on H100; a linked issue says the K=0 draft-state forward costs 4-11%.
does_not_prove: Author's own measurements, not independently verified; no setup detail in fetch. Does not say what catch-up would cost instead.
bearing: C3' supports: always-sync at K=0 has a real tax, motivating lazy/windowed catch-up

title: [Performance]: Dynamic speculative decoding (num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size) causes catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse ... (vllm #49548)
quote: the K=0 step count data (82.6% at 4-session) — correct, verified.
proves: 1321 of 1600 steps (82.6%) were K=0 at 4 sessions (dual RTX 5090, 35B-A3B MoE, MTP).
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED (partly): "K=0 runs of 5-15 steps" is only a self-reported aside ("our data shows avg 5-15 steps") with no run-length data published. The 82.6% is on different hardware from the original GB10 report; the H3 attribution was later retracted.
bearing: C3' supports: K=0 is the common case under concurrency, so resume events are frequent

title: [Perf] DSD arms pay a large baseline tax vs no-spec under production defaults; PIECEWISE override identified as one factor (vllm #49986)
quote: The -35% gap at 32k context on the 27B dense is currently unexplained.
proves: Aug 9 table, dual RTX 5090, 8 sessions, always-K=0 (C2) vs no-spec (C1): -7.9% (27B dense short), -8.7% (35B MoE short), -35.1% (27B dense 32k), -21.9% (35B MoE 32k).
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED as stated: the span is 7.9-35.1%, not 8.7-35.1%; numbers are 3-5-round point estimates; later HTTP runs gave -15.2%/-5.7% (MoE) and corrected dense -5.1%/-20.5% after a stale-override retraction; H100 Gemma-4 showed +6.56% TPOT not growing with context.
bearing: C3' supports with caveats: K=0 tax real but size unstable

title: [Bug]: EAGLE / MTP Doesn't Overwrite Approximated Hidden States / KV Cache, 8%- 15% Acceptance Length Degradation (vllm #14649)
quote: in vLLM, we never overwrite EAGLE's approximated KV cache if the drafted token is accepted.

does_not_prove: Author's measurement only; closed when maintainer believed EAGLE3/MTP correctness issues were resolved without measuring. Not about K=0 resume.
bearing: C3' supports: stale draft state measurably costs acceptance; C7' shows acceptance as a bug signal

title: Ekka: Automated Diagnosis of Silent Errors in LLM Inference

proves: Ekka aligns and compares intermediate states between a target and reference framework to find root causes of silent errors; benchmark of 17 real errors.

does_not_prove: Several implementations, not all. Ragged-tensor batching bugs, not K=0 resume or draft-state catch-up.

does_not_prove: Within-step depth effect, not stale or windowed draft KV after K=0.
